subject: Log lineage and custody: export formats & redaction options
messages:
From: Alyssa Cohen <alyssa@blueriver.health>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: BlueRiver Health Security <security@blueriver.health>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Request: log lineage and custody for upcoming SOC2 review

Rafael —

Thanks for taking this. As part of our SOC 2 readiness audit we need a formal description of what you log for admin/operator actions, how long those records are retained, and an in-scope export we can provide to our auditors. Specifically they asked for: 
- a manifest enumerating exported files with checksums and record counts
- proof of chain-of-custody (signed manifest or HMAC)
- options for redacting PII or sampling if retention windows exceed what we need

High level constraints: auditors want an initial bundle covering 2025-07-01 through 2025-12-31, plus a daily incremental snapshot for January 2026. We expect the bundle to include role changes, console logins, API key rotations, and operator actions (restarts, scale events).

Can you confirm what we can deliver, which fields are included in each event, and an estimated delivery ETA?

Thanks,
Alyssa
Alyssa Cohen
Security Lead — BlueRiver Health
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Cohen <alyssa@blueriver.health>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: log lineage and custody for upcoming SOC2 review

Alyssa —

Appreciate the clear scope. We can provide the bundle you described. Quick summary of what we will include by default and a couple of options you can choose from: 

Default bundle (no extra configuration, available for all customers):
- admin_events.csv: role_grants/revokes, user_create/delete, permission_changes
- access_log.csv: console logins (timestamp, user, source IP, MFA flag)
- operator_events.csv: node_restarts, pod_evictions, autoscaler decisions (with service id)
- manifest.csv: filename, sha256, record_count, start_ts, end_ts

Retention & availability:
- Default retention: 180 days for parsed CSV-level admin/operator events
- Extended retention: 12 months available under enterprise plans (we can enable an off-site archive)
- Raw operator traces (debug-level logs) are retained for 90 days and can be included in an evidence bundle on request (larger size, different delivery options)

Export formats & custody options:
1) Signed manifest bundle (preferred for audits): we provide a .tar.gz with CSVs + manifest.csv + manifest.sig (HMAC-SHA256 using our export key). Delivery via short-lived S3 presigned URL or secure SFTP.
2) Incremental S3 snapshots: daily delta files pushed to an S3 bucket we provision (transfer logs + manifest per day). We can provide cross-account access or presigned URLs.
3) Live SIEM ingest: if you want Splunk/Datadog ingest, we can set up a forwarding pipeline; note this does not provide the same immutable bundle but can be used for continuous monitoring.

Field notes (things auditors often ask about):
- We include request_id, user_id (Redwood internal id), user_email (if applicable), action, target_resource, ip, region, and result (success/fail).
- KV cache eviction events are not currently surfaced in the admin_events CSV; we can add them, but they will lengthen the bundle and include low-level runtime noise.
- IAM policy snapshots are exported as a separate file (iam_snapshot.json) if you want effective permissions at a point-in-time.

ETA: We can produce a first attested bundle for 2025-07-01 -> 2025-12-31 in 48 business hours once we have an SFTP endpoint or confirmation to use presigned S3. Daily incrementals for Jan 2026 can be staged starting next-day after access is validated.

I'll loop in Soojin from Security to confirm HMAC/signing details and redaction mechanics. Do you prefer S3 presigned links or an SFTP drop?

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Alyssa Cohen <alyssa@blueriver.health>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: log lineage and custody for upcoming SOC2 review

Alyssa / Rafael —

Adding some implementation details and proposed checklist so auditors have a clear trail:

What we will include in the delivered bundle (attached: sample_manifest.tsv):
- manifest.tsv (tab-separated): file | sha256 | records | compressed_size_bytes | start_ts | end_ts
- admin_events.csv: timestamp, request_id, actor_email, actor_id, action, resource_type, resource_id, change_summary
- access_log.csv: timestamp, user_email, session_id, ip, ua, mfa_present, auth_result
- operator_events.csv: timestamp, node_id, service, event_type, details (JSON blob)
- iam_snapshot.json (optional if you want point-in-time perms)

Signing/chain-of-custody:
- We will generate manifest.tsv and sign it with an HMAC-SHA256 key. We maintain an audit of export requests (who requested, who approved). For attestation we can provide the public fingerprint of the signing key and an export approval email thread.

Redaction & sampling options:
- PII redaction: we can redact email addresses and IPs (replace with hashed tokens) for exported bundles. This is irreversible for the exported artifact.
- Sampling: we can provide 10%/25%/100% sampling for operator_events if you want smaller bundles for early review. Sampling is uniform and seedable for repeatability.

Delivery & verification steps (recommended):
1) You provide S3 bucket ARN (cross-account) or SFTP creds.
2) We stage the bundle to a presigned URL / SFTP and generate manifest.tsv + manifest.sig.
3) You verify checksums and we provide the HMAC fingerprint and our internal export approval log.
4) We retain a copy for 7 days post-delivery to support any re-check requests; after that the bundle is purged unless you requested an extension.

Attachments: log_handoff_playbook_v2.pdf (procedural playbook), sample_manifest.tsv

If that looks good, Rafael — please advise on the default redaction setting (none vs hash emails/IPs) and confirm S3 vs SFTP. Alyssa — if you want us to redact email addresses by default, say so and we will produce the redacted bundle first.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Security Compliance — Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Cohen <alyssa@blueriver.health>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: log lineage and custody for upcoming SOC2 review

Alyssa —

Thanks — per Soojin's note we will: 
- Produce the signed .tar.gz with CSVs + manifest.tsv + manifest.sig
- Apply email/IP hashing redaction by default for the first bundle (we'll provide a non-redacted bundle only with an approved DPA amendment)
- Deliver via presigned S3 URLs (we will send one-time links to the security@blueriver.health address)

Action items & timeline:
- Alyssa: confirm presigned-S3 is acceptable and provide preferred S3 target or give us permission to create a temporary bucket (cross-account).
- Blake (BlueRiver security alias): expect an email from export@redwood.com with the first presigned link in ~48 business hours after confirmation.
- Redwood: we'll create a JIRA ticket (JIRA-3456) for the export job, include checksums and the export approval audit trail.

Referenced links:
- Evidence playbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/fakeLink123
- JIRA: JIRA-3456

If you confirm S3 we will start the job today.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
